display.purpose: The empty-state heading only. One per screen, and most screens have none.

title.purpose: Panel headings, node titles, the wordmark's size peer.

body.purpose: Conversation messages and the composer. The lane caps at 860px so the measure stays readable when the graph pane is collapsed.

micro.purpose: Measurements, counts, provenance, status. The densest and most-used size in the app.

wordmark.purpose: "Zephyr" in the nav, uppercased via CSS text-transform so the accessible name is not spelled out letter by letter.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default.

motion.name: reflow
motion.purpose: Opening the inspector. Animating the grid is what makes selection read as the layout reflowing rather than a panel landing on top of the graph.

motion.name: node-state
motion.purpose: A trace node becoming real. All four properties move together so the change is legible as a transition rather than a repaint.

motion.name: field-focus
motion.purpose: The composer border lifting to mark-strong, so the field lights up as one object.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The only filled-accent control on a screen. Starting a run, sending, approving.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 14px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 7px; font: 500 11px/1.5 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.2px; color: var(--accent-ink, #182116); background: var(--accent, #d0dfb5); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--accent-bright, #deedbf); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #d0dfb5); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Everything that is not the one primary action. Accent-tinted type, never an accent fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line-3, #2f3b2c); border-radius: 7px; font: 500 11px/1.5 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.2px; color: var(--accent-text-2, #d0ddbd); background: var(--surface-3, #1d231d); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--line-2, #2b3425); border-color: var(--accent-line, #5f7a54); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #d0dfb5); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: Transparent at rest; the ground appears only on hover. Used for close, expand, fit-to-view.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-icon" aria-label="Close decision detail"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M18 6 6 18M6 6l12 12"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-icon { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--accent-text, #c0d2a9); border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-icon:hover { background: var(--hover, #1f2720); color: var(--text, #e9eee7); } .ds-btn-icon:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #d0dfb5); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Composer
components.description: The task field. The container carries the border and the focus state, so the field lights up as one object.
components.css: .ds-composer { border: 1px solid var(--line-4, #3c4b31); border-radius: 13px; background: var(--raised-panel, #1a1f1c); overflow: hidden; transition: border-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-composer:focus-within { border-color: var(--mark-strong, #afc294); } .ds-composer textarea { width: 100%; border: 0; background: transparent; resize: vertical; min-height: 65px; max-height: 180px; color: var(--text, #e9eee7); padding: 17px 18px 5px; font: 400 13px/1.65 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; outline: none; caret-color: var(--accent, #d0dfb5); } .ds-composer textarea::placeholder { color: var(--secondary, #b0b9b0); }

components.name: Metrics Strip
components.description: The fixed measurement floor. It spans the full width and never scrolls away — on an instrument panel the gauges do not leave the frame.

narrative.overview:
Zephyr is the glass cockpit for a running agent. The person using it is not browsing a product; they are watching a machine work and deciding whether to let it continue. So the interface behaves like instrumentation: dark, dense, unlit except where there is something to report, and absolutely literal about what it knows. Nothing here is decorative, because on an instrument panel a light that means nothing is a defect.

The whole visual system is one idea — brightness is evidence. The canvas is the darkest thing in the app and everything rises off it in a fixed order: unexecuted structure barely above the ground, materialized work above that, the accent reserved for the single thing that is live or chosen. There are no shadows anywhere in this system. Depth is entirely tonal, which is why the ladder is generated rather than hand-written: one hand-edited value puts a surface on the wrong rung and the reading breaks silently.

The five worlds (sage, slate, ember, mono, daylight) are the same ladder re-hued in OKLCH at constant lightness. Changing theme changes the hue of the instrument, never its architecture. daylight is the one deliberate exception: on a light ground "canvas is darkest" cannot hold, so it inverts to "canvas is quietest, executed work is most inked" — the rule underneath survives, which is the part that matters.
keyCharacteristics: A generated OKLCH luminance ladder, identical across every dark world
Zero shadows; depth is tonal layering only
One typeface, no monospace — measurement is a size and weight, not a costume
The accent appears on the live, selected, or chosen thing and nowhere else
Unknown measurements render an em dash, never 0
Planned structure is dim and dashed; it never borrows the appearance of executed work

rules.name: The Ladder Rule
rules.body: Every dark world is the same OKLCH lightness ladder, re-hued. Tokens are generated by tools/theme/generate.mjs and spliced into src/workspace.css. Hand-edit one value and you break the invariant tests/theme.test.mjs exists to protect — regenerate instead.

rules.name: The One Bright Thing Rule
rules.body: accent and accent-bright mark what is live, selected, or chosen. They are never used to make a section look important.

rules.name: The Sealed Blocks Rule
rules.body: No color literal may appear anywhere outside the theme blocks at the top of src/workspace.css. A test enforces it. A one-off hex is how a ladder dies.

rules.name: The Signal Invariance Rule
rules.body: Amber and alarm rose do not re-hue with the theme. A person who learns "amber means a human is needed" in sage must not have to relearn it in ember.

rules.name: The No Costume Rule
rules.body: There is no monospace face in this system. Numbers are distinguished by size, weight and color, not by pretending to be code. Use a tabular variant if digits jitter; do not reach for a mono family.

rules.name: The Em Dash Rule
rules.body: An unknown measurement renders an em dash. It never renders 0, -, n/a or an empty cell. A measured zero renders 0 and must remain distinguishable from unknown.

rules.name: The Canvas Floor Rule
rules.body: In every dark world, canvas is the darkest surface in the app and nothing may sit below it. In daylight the rule inverts to its light-ground equivalent: canvas is the quietest surface and executed work carries the most ink.

rules.name: The Recessive Plan Rule
rules.body: Planned structure sits below materialized work on the ladder in all five worlds, daylight included. Dimming is not a styling preference here; it is the visual form of "we have not observed this yet."

dos: Do regenerate the theme with node tools/theme/generate.mjs and python tools/theme/splice.py, then run node --test "tests/*.test.mjs". Never hand-edit a token.
Do place a new surface on an existing rung of the ladder and give it the matching 1px line-* border.
Do render an unknown measurement as an em dash, and keep a measured 0 distinguishable from it.
Do spend the accent on exactly one thing per screen: the live, selected, or chosen item.
Do keep planned structure recessive and dashed in all five worlds, daylight included.
Do label provenance truthfully — live, mock, fixture and replay are four different things and must look like it.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces (selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring) from the palette.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. This system has none; depth is tonal.
Don't write a color literal outside the theme blocks in src/workspace.css. A test fails on it, and the ladder is the reason.
Don't introduce a monospace face to make numbers look technical.
Don't re-hue amber or alarm rose per theme; their constancy is what makes them readable.
Don't give a planned node measurements, or let it borrow the appearance of executed work.
Don't put a permanent navigation rail back. The drawer exists so the graph keeps the width.
Don't use border weight above 1px for emphasis; move the line up a rung instead.
Don't silently fall back to preview behaviour on a live run — a failed live request shows as an error, never as a successful mock.
